title: LLM inference serving, Part 4: PagedAttention
tldr: How a server manages KV cache memory like virtual memory: why reserving each request's cache for its maximum length wastes most of it (the vLLM paper's reserved slots, internal and external fragmentation, and its 20.4% to 38.2% measurement), fixed-size KV blocks with per-request block tables and the operating-system page-table mapping and where it breaks, how attention reads scattered blocks, copy-on-write sharing in the 2023 paper versus automatic prefix caching in vLLM v0.31.0 (block hashes, reference counts, LRU eviction), how gpu_memory_utilization and block size set the block pool, preemption by recompute when blocks run out, multi-tenant cache traps, a step-through block pool, a fragmentation calculator, a tested toy allocator, honest backend analogies and an interview drill.
